figures.title: A variable declaration and what it reserves in memory
figures.description: The declaration double pointsEarned equals 84.5 is shown above a diagram of memory. An arrow labelled name points from the identifier to a block of eight shaded memory cells at addresses 4000 through 4007. A label reads: the type double decides that eight bytes are reserved and how the bits in them are interpreted. A second label notes that the name is how your program refers to that location, and the value 84.5 is what is stored there.
